svg.title: Prithvi Raghu: research and selected work
svg.desc: Prithvi Raghu: I study quantum circuits for ML, games and option pricing, plus HF radio geolocation. Open to research collaborations. Quantum games: 98% of the ideal GHZ payoff gain kept on real IBM hardware, 3–5 players (first author; after error mitigation; below random at 6–7 players). Quantum ML: 1 measurement, at the end; its unitary pooling provably matches measured pooling (co-author; simulated, 10 qubits; below classical, above tensor-network; none significant). Option pricing: 50× fewer qubits via reflection than the project’s arithmetic design, but 3.1× the CX gates (draft; ideal estimates, no hardware; in a second case, reflection needs fewer CX). HF geolocation: 25% lower mean error than physics alone, 103 to 77 km (solo; simulated emitters, noise-free angles, one site, 2012 data; 6.5% gain in storms).
